A canvas-grammar seed can be fully live-evidenced AND still have no honest rendering behind it — the answer is to port the landing grammar and make the un-renderable region a typed absence that distinguishes MISSING from the reference's own EMPTY, never to draw a plausible picture and never to downgrade the seed back to absent. REG-1 SHIPPED registry (the third of this backlog) and returned the finding the remaining legs must carry: when the estate DOES have the plane, the honest work is DISCRIMINATION rather than absence. Probe each lane's plane over the surface's own identity and classify from the response itself — a typed refusal, an empty collection and a plane with no read route are three different truths and NONE of them is a zero. Rendering an identity-first refusal as “0 records” is the same defect class as drawing a plausible map: it converts a closed door into a measurement the estate never took. JOB-1 SHIPPED jobs (the fourth of this backlog) and returned the finding the remaining legs must carry: when several planes project the SAME records, the work is not picking the biggest one but asking which projection is COMPLETE and which fields each one carries. Here two projections of one plane were each incomplete AND each missing a field the other had (the transcript plane: a state_root on every record and a principal on none; the per-automation projection: a principal, no state root, and no reach at all to executions whose automation was deleted) — and the union plane that carried both had to be found before a single row could be rendered honestly. Re-derive the reach counts on every render so the plane choice can never rot into a stale justification, and LINK a plane that another surface already renders rather than minting a second renderer over the same records. SCH-1 SHIPPED scheduler (the fifth of this backlog) and returned the finding the remaining legs must carry: a number is not a measurement until you know the PREDICATE that produced it and the WINDOW it covers, and the field that carries the concept's NAME is routinely not the one the runtime acts on. Here the scheduler loop admits on `enabled && schedule_is_active(schedule_spec)` and never reads `trigger`, so the automation it fires on a cron reads trigger_kind: manual and a trigger-shaped view would have reported zero schedules while the loop fired one; a second projection of the same census admits by a different predicate again (it never reads `enabled`); and two of the three counters the surface would naturally put in its header are reset every tick, so printing them as totals would convert a 15-second window into a history exactly as printing a refusal as 0 converts a closed door into a measurement. Read a field's DEFINITION from the code or route that WRITES it, never from its name, print the predicate and the window beside every number, and where another component owns a predicate, link its own count rather than re-deriving the test in a read surface — a re-implemented admission rule is a second answer waiting to disagree with the first.
